sources_considered.why: Primary press release for a large 2026 enterprise survey that reports the share seeing significant ROI from AI agents.
Reuters report of Gartner's June 2025 assessment that most agentic AI propositions lack significant value or ROI. The Gartner page itself returned HTTP 403.
Primary PwC survey from May 2025 in which two-thirds of agent adopters report measurable productivity value. This is counterevidence.
Secondary summary of Google Cloud's 2025 ROI of AI study. Other coverage says the 88% figure refers to gen AI ROI on at least one use case, so I use it as context only.

evidence_items.locator: section 'The top AI adoption challenges facing the C-suite', Lagging ROI bullet

receipt.public_excerpt: Still, few leaders say they’ve seen significant ROI from generative AI (29%) or AI agents (23%), and nearly half (48%) feel that AI adoption at their company has been a massive disappointment.

evidence_items.explanation: In a survey of 2,400 workers and executives (fieldwork Dec 2025 to Jan 2026), only 23% of leaders reported significant ROI from AI agents. This fits 'not so much ROI' for agents and matches the pattern for gen AI. The publisher is a vendor that sells agents.

receipt.public_excerpt: "Most agentic AI propositions lack significant value or return on investment, as current models do not have the maturity and agency to autonomously achieve complex business goals or follow nuanced instructions over time," Verma said.

evidence_items.explanation: A Gartner analyst said most agentic AI offerings lacked significant value or ROI. In the same piece she said most projects were 'mostly driven by hype'. This supports both halves of the claim for mid-2025.

evidence_items.locator: section 'Key trends about AI agents in the enterprise', paragraph 2

receipt.public_excerpt: Seventy-nine percent say AI agents are already being adopted in their companies. And of those adopting AI agents, two-thirds (66%) say that they’re delivering measurable value through increased productivity.

evidence_items.explanation: Two-thirds of US agent adopters said agents deliver measurable productivity value. That cuts against 'not so much ROI' if any measurable value counts. PwC also says this 'stops short of transformation'. The available_at date is approximate: the page says the survey ran in May 2025.

receipt.public_excerpt: The second annual AI ROI study reveals 88% of agentic AI early adopters achieve positive return on investment, with 52% of generative AI organizations now deploying AI agents in production environments

evidence_items.explanation: A secondary summary of Google Cloud's vendor study reports high positive ROI among agent 'early adopters', who made up a minority of respondents. Other coverage says the figure refers to gen AI ROI on at least one use case, so I treat it as context only.

unresolved_gaps: No independent, audited measure of agent ROI exists. All the surveys rely on self-reports, and several come from vendors.
I could not read the McKinsey State of AI 2025 page or the Gartner primary release. Both timed out or were blocked.
The Anthropic 2026 State of AI Agents report (said to find 80% see returns) could not be read or dated against the post.
The surveys use different thresholds ('significant ROI', 'measurable value', 'positive ROI on at least one use case'), so they cannot be directly compared.
